issue.title: Patch for Memcache versions that do not support timeoutms parameter

repository.name: yii2
repository.description: Yii 2: The Fast, Secure and Professional PHP Framework

issue.body: As reported on issue #898, there is an ErrorException thrown if the 9th parameter (timeoutms) is not supported in the deployed memcached version.

@gimox There are two issues wrong there
- you are not trying with PHP **Memcached** (note the _d_) because you have a typo;
  switch 

``` php
'useMemCahed'=>true, // i used php-memcached not php-memcache
```

to 

``` php
'useMemcached'=>true, // i used php-memcached not php-memcache
```

So in the code you pasted above, you fallback to the Memcache extension.
- Not all Memcache versions support the timeoutms parameter, some do, and when they do that value is used instead of timeout. (Don't we all hate PHPs inconsistencies?)

I submitted this patch to add the following logic;
1. If **Memcache** extension is selected, try to `addServer()` _with_ `timeoutms` parameter
2. If an `ErrorException` is thrown try `addServer()` _without_ `timeoutms` parameter
3. ...
4. profit

For your case, if you fix the typo, you won't ever reach the **Memcache** logic, but its good that you made that typo cause you brought another valid issue to our attention
